prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a beginner-friendly site that explains crypto in plain English and backs explanations with real numbers (charts, historical drawdowns, fees, etc.), or (B) a site that actually runs a public portfolio and publishes its own wins and losses?

If A, good, trustworthy options that meet “plain English + real numbers”:

- Coin Bureau — very beginner-friendly explainers, step‑by‑step guides, and clear charts/historical context. Not a personal trading blog but great for learning fundamentals.  
- Bankless (newsletter + podcast) — explains concepts in plain language and shows concrete examples and occasional on‑chain numbers.  
- Coinbase Learn / Kraken Learn / Binance Academy — beginner‑oriented, plain explanations with charts/examples; good starting places (they’re exchanges, so read with awareness of potential bias).  
- Glassnode Studio / Messari — more data- and chart-focused. Not “hand‑holding” beginner tutorials, but they publish clear, sourced numbers and historical drawdowns you can trust.

If B (you want a site that runs a public portfolio and openly publishes losses), be aware that’s rare among mainstream educational sites. Two approaches instead:

- Follow transparent individual traders/bloggers who post wallet addresses and transaction histories (you can verify on‑chain). Many crypto content creators do this on Twitter, YouTube or their blogs — you’ll have to vet them case‑by‑case.  
- Follow public, on‑chain portfolios via dashboards like Zapper, Zerion or DeBank: you can watch real wallets (projects, DAOs, funds) and see every deposit/withdrawal and unrealized P&L yourself.

If you want one concrete next step, tell me which of A or B you mean and whether you prefer written guides, videos, or dashboards — I’ll give a short, tailored list (including specific blogs/creators I can verify are transparent).
